added_lines: mon - wed. 9.00am - 12. 30pm the society for the propagation of the faith was founded in 1822 by a french laywoman, pauline jaricot. she wished to help not only french missions and missionaries but all missions and missionaries especially the poorest. in 1922 the society for the propagation of the faith became the primary organisation of the church for supporting the activity of the missionaries. pope pius x1 instituted mission sunday in 1926 and ordered that it be observed in a ll churches and oratories throughout the world as a day of prayer and material support for missionary activity. it was pauline who drew up the basic plan of the society. it is one of prayer, offering up of suffering and making a financial contribution for the spread of the faith. this year the theme chosen by pope leo is "one in christ, united in mission" “holiness and mission are inescapable aspects of the vocation of every baptised person. the commitment to become more holy is clearly linked to that of spreading the message of salvation. every member of the faithful is called to holiness and to mission.” mission is not over. many of the young churches eva ngelised are now producing missionaries to other young churches. many of these young churches are rich in vocations but poor in financial resources. all financial contributions for mission sunday go directly to the missions. it assists missionaries to” make his face shine “before the millions who have never had the opportunity to hear about or see the face of christ. it is the one day in the year that pope leo asks your extra generosity on this day, collections will be taken up throughout the world and used to help support missionaries who bring faith, hope and love to those who are suffering on this day, your generosity will ultimately help build churches, hospitals, schools and vocations in countries where the church is too young or poor to support itself. the family of parishes of: ballincollig | the irish cancer society the society is seeking compassionate volunteer drivers to join our pool of drivers. as a volunteer driver you would be bringing patient undergoing chemotherapy to the hospital and back home for their treatment. gifting your time means that cancer patients will have comfortable (one on one) transport to attend appointments for their lifesaving treatment. if you can spare 2 days per month, have a valid driving licence, and a safe, reliable vehicle, you are the perfect candidate to make a significant difference. the irish cancer society will provide you with training before you start as a driver fous. your generosity not only eases the journey for many during a challenging time but also offers comfort and support when it's needed most. for more information and to become a volunteer driver, please contact monica or emily at
